finish.summary:
I built a small three-cell sewing caddy that fits on a tabletop. It has three parts:
- **Front row:** two divided bins. One has 3 compartments and the other has 2, so thread, buttons, pins and other notions can each have their own spot.
- **Raised cell:** a second-storey cell over the middle with a full-depth open bin, for scissors, chalk and fabric pens.
- **Pull-out drawer:** a drawer frame in the gap between the two front cells (the configurator lists it as a notch drawer, not a regular drawer), for needles and pins.

All open faces are capped and the joints are bolted, and the configurator's checks found no problems or collisions.

The catalog has no sewing props, so I staged it with a pen and a marker standing up to show the use. A pencil and a tape measure wouldn't stay in place, so I left them out.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
